Verbs in -ere

You already know the verbs in -are: parlo, parli, parla… Verbs in -ere work the same way: remove -ere and add the ending. Good news: for io, tu and noi, the endings are the same as for -are.

parlareprendere
ioparloprendo
tuparliprendi
lui / leiparlaprende
noiparliamoprendiamo
voiparlateprendete
loroparlanoprendono

Where English just adds an -s for he/she (I take, she takes), Italian has an ending for every person — but the pattern stays regular: prendo, prendiamo, prendono. Same for reading, writing, living: leggo, scrivo, vivo.

La sera Marco legge e Anna scrive.In the evening, Marco reads and Anna writes.

Pronunciation

Before o, a, u, the g is hard (as in \"go\"); before e and i, it is soft (as in \"gem\"). So leggo sounds like \"LEG-go\", but leggi and legge sound like \"LED-jee\", \"LED-jeh\". In scrivo, you clearly hear all three consonants: \"skree-vo\".

With loro, the stress stays at the start of the verb: prendono is said \"PREN-do-no\", like parlano. Never \"pren-DO-no\".

", "

Verbs in -ire: two families

Verbs in -ire have almost the same endings as -ere; only voi changes: -ite. But some of them add -isc- between the stem and the ending.

dormirecapire
iodormocapisco
tudormicapisci
lui / leidormecapisce
noidormiamocapiamo
voidormitecapite
lorodormonocapiscono
  • Like dormire: partire, sentire, aprire, offrire.
  • Like capire: finire, preferire, pulire.

The trap: -isc- appears with io, tu, lui / lei and loro, but disappears with noi and voi (finiamo, finite). In the table, it draws a \"boot\" shape: the top three rows and the last one.

Nothing in the infinitive tells you whether a verb takes -isc-: learn each verb with its io form (capire, capisco). For pronunciation, sc sounds like \"sk\" before o (capisco, capiscono) and like \"sh\" before i and e (capisci, capisce).

", "

The three groups at a glance

-are-ere-ire
io-o-o-o / -isco
tu-i-i-i / -isci
lui / lei-a-e-e / -isce
noi-iamo-iamo-iamo
voi-ate-ete-ite
loro-ano-ono-ono / -iscono

The rule in one sentence: io, tu and noi have the same endings in all three groups (adding -isc- for capire, finire…), and voi keeps the vowel of the infinitive (parlate, prendete, dormite).

A few meanings to remember

  • vivere and abitare: Vivo a Parigi = Abito a Parigi (I live in Paris).
  • sentire means to hear, but also to feel or to smell: Sento la musica (I hear the music).
  • chiedere = to ask, rispondere = to answer, credere = to believe.

At the café, among friends: Offro io! It's on me!

title: Verbs in -ere and -ire
topic: present tense of regular -ere and -ire verbs, including the -isc- group
why: After -are verbs, the learner completes the regular present, slowly and with lots of reuse: the other two groups, the -isc- family and the pronunciation of leggo / leggi, around the theme of free time and habits.
